records.question: What does the text say about prior permission for UNIFIL to carry out mandated tasks?
source: Operative paragraph 1 extended UNIFIL's existing mandate until 31 August 2024. Paragraph 15 reaffirmed its independence in carrying out mandated tasks without prior permission and its continued coordination with Lebanon's Government under the status-of-forces agreement.

On 31 August 2023 in meeting S/PV.9409, the Council voted on draft S/2023/641 submitted by France. It was adopted as resolution 2695 (2023) by 13 votes in favour and none against, with China and the Russian Federation abstaining. Brazil voted in favour.
source_withheld: Russia attributed its abstention to contentious late drafting changes and said the final text lost a prior compromise. It continued to support the mission's activities and called for coordination with Lebanon's Government.

records.question: What did resolution 2704 do about Government–EMC monitoring and verification?
values: Expressed willingness to consider later under conditions
source: S/PV.9461, p. 2. Ghana spoke on behalf of the three African members. The A3 welcomed the unanimous mandate extension, supported Mission monitoring and verification in the EMC case contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, and pledged to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people.

Resolution 2704, final preambular paragraph. Resolution 2694 had already extended the Mission's role to monitoring and verification of the Government–ELN ceasefire. Resolution 2704 expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification when the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with appropriate verification protocols and taking into account his update on implementation of resolution 2694.
source_withheld: S/PV.9461, p. 2. Ghana spoke on behalf of the three African members. The A3 welcomed the unanimous mandate extension, supported Mission monitoring and verification in the EMC case contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, and pledged to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people.

S/PV.9461, p. 2. On 30 October 2023, the Council voted on United Kingdom draft S/2023/808. All 15 members voted in favour and the Council President announced unanimous adoption as resolution 2704 (2023).
faithful: Resolution 2704 expressed willingness to consider monitoring and verification of a Government–EMC ceasefire under conditions.
foil: Resolution 2704 immediately granted the Mission authority to monitor and verify a Government–EMC ceasefire.
records.source_witness: expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification

records.question: In what capacity did the representative say the Council should respond to Colombia's priorities?
values: As Council President speaking for the Council
source: Resolution 2704, final preambular paragraph. Resolution 2694 had already extended the Mission's role to monitoring and verification of the Government–ELN ceasefire. Resolution 2704 expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification when the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with appropriate verification protocols and taking into account his update on implementation of resolution 2694.

S/PV.9461, p. 3. The presiding representative switched to speaking for Brazil. He said the Council should respond to Colombia's priorities as expressed by its Government and described the resolution as reflecting Colombia's sovereign will. Brazil supported the Government's total peace strategy and hoped the Council could authorize verification of the EMC ceasefire when sufficiently mature.
